title: Begging his stepfather to let him carry plaster
summary: He asked to help his stepfather's plastering job, cried when refused, and was allowed to carry half a bucket.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers

blocks.x: When you started out as a pastor, did you have to be sort of an apprentice and all for a long time?

Oh yes, I had to be an apprentice. I'll tell you what happened. My stepfather was contracting for himself. And we were living then on Telemachus between Borden and Henry Court. And that section wasn't well built up then. It just began to build that section up.
Louis Nelson lives up there now. The commonwealth is in that. On that street, I guess it's almost the same section.
I guess so. And you know where Jefferson Davis? Yeah. We were at Telemachus. It's three blocks towards the lake.
And Borden, this is Tulane Avenue, Henry Court and Borden. Borden's two blocks towards Canal Street.

Then, uh, then from Banks Street, which is the next street from Borden, three blocks. From Banks on down to, uh, Cleveland. Banks, Palmyne, Cleveland. All that was vacancies, vacant lots out there. Mm-hmm. And a fella by the name of Jake Curran was a builder at that time. And, uh, he was buying those lots out there and billing houses and selling them. Uh, and, uh, my stepfather was this classroom. So, on a Saturday, my stepdaddy had, uh, wound up a job, with the exception of, uh, kitchen and bathroom bottoms. They used to do the wainscoting instead of tile, like, uh, people do now.
They used to plaster it and cut imitation tiles and paint them. Yes, I'm kidding.
Because they're not around here. You remember that?

So, my stepdaddy had two, and there's two, two bottoms to do. The kitchen bottom and the bathroom bottom. So, uh, mother sent me over there to bring him some breakfast. Just about two blocks from home. And, uh, I brought the breakfast all that time and he was working by himself. So, uh, I said, pops, I said, anybody working with you? He said, no. I said, who's carrying the stuff? He, this white finishing, you know, he's carrying the stuff. He said, I'm carrying myself. He said, why don't you let me come back and carry it for you? He says, uh, oh boy, you're too small, yeah? He said, too small. Well, that thing went to my horse because he would let me carry this stuff. And I went back home, and I looked so funny. I said, what's the matter, son? And I broke down and cried. I said, pop, don't let me carry that stuff for him over there. Let me carry it. I said, you go back there and tell him, I said, let you carry it if you don't care about a spoonful. See? So, boy, I flew back there. I was so happy. I said, pop, I said, mama, you let me carry some of that stuff. I don't care about a spoonful. I said, oh man, I laughed. He said, all right. He said, if it don't take about a half a bucket, he said, man. Well, I was strong enough to carry a bucket. It's like lying, you know. I said, okay. So, I take a carry a half a bucket, I get another half a bucket, dump it in that bucket, make a bucket full, you know. So, I was the happiest thing in the world then, man.
